- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after recent spikes.  
- If official event net is bearish (supply_net < 0) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for supply pressure.  
- If sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and forecast is rising, apply downward bias to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to allow mean reversion.  
- When official events are frequent (≥15 events/30d) and supply_net is negative, forecast should be anchored to 1–2% below recent 18-day average to reflect volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should not assume linear trend — apply smoothing filter to avoid overfitting to recent highs.  
- For low-event periods (≤5 events/30d), forecast should be more stable and less volatile — avoid sharp upward revisions unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
